section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the intrinsic love of Hashem for the souls of Israel, He sends His hand from the hole, opening the way for the four levels of "my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one," corresponding to the four letters of the Name Havayah, which manifest as light, joy, gladness, and honor.
section.t: And regarding this, the verse continues,
"My beloved sent his hand from the hole,"
meaning that although the Holy Spirit responds in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, "I have washed my feet, how can I defile them?" etc.,
nevertheless, from the aspect of the matter of "my beloved sent his hand,"
where "my beloved" refers to the intrinsic love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for the souls of Israel
(and as the Alter Rebbe explains in the maamar on the verse "I arose to open for my beloved,"
and it is explained in the sicha of the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory27),
and from the aspect of intrinsic love,
behold, "He sent his hand from the hole,"
where "hole" (chor) is also related to the term "fine linen" (chur) and also to the term "freedom" (cheirus)28,
and through this, "Open for me" is brought about,
and after "Open for me," the four levels of "my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one,"
which are four levels both in the service regarding love,
for there is no worship like the worship of love29,
and in the service of fulfilling the commandments,
for these four levels correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah30,
and through this, "For the Jews there was light, and joy, and gladness, and honor"31,
and it can be said that the four matters of light, joy, etc., correspond to the four letters of the Name Havayah,
for "light" is Torah32,
and as it is written33,
"For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light,"
which is the aspect of the Sefirah of Chochmah,
"joy" is the aspect of the Festivals32,
for joy,
which is the aspect of the Sefirah of Binah,
and "gladness" is circumcision32,
which is the aspect of the Sefirah of Yesod, which is the main part of Zeir Anpin,
and "honor" is Tefillin32,
which are the aspect of Malchus, as explained at the end of Shaarei Orah34,
and as it is in its root in the Essence (Atzmus) of Ein Sof, blessed be He,
which is what is said in the Zohar Chadash35,
that Tefillin are the likeness of the seal of the Supreme King,
for "likeness" and "seal" are the aspect of the Sefirah of Malchus,
meaning that through "Open for me," the four letters of the Name Havayah are drawn into service,
and likewise into the light, joy, etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that a Jew is defined by self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh), as exemplified by Mordechai, and that this self-sacrifice, which is beyond intellect, draws down the four letters of Havayah—light, joy, gladness, and honor—even into the lowest physical realm.
section.t: And this is also what is written, "For the Jews there was light, etc.," and as it is stated in the Gemara36,
that anyone who denies idolatry is called a Jew,
meaning that first there is the matter of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh), with which they stood at that time in the days of Purim,
and this is the aspect of "Open for me like the eye of a needle," which is the aspect of self-sacrifice,
and afterwards come the four levels of light, joy, gladness, and honor,
and this is also what is written37,
"There was a Jewish man in Shushan the capital, and his name was Mordechai,"
for Mordechai—from where in the Torah? As it is said38,
"Mar Dror" (pure myrrh),
and we translate it as "Mira Dakhya"39,
and as explained in Torah Or40,
and "Jew" (Yehudi) is the aspect of self-sacrifice as above,
for "Yehudi" is from the term "thanksgiving" (hoda'ah), which is above intellect and reason,

and this affected in all of them the matter of self-sacrifice, so that they are all specifically called "Jews," as per the Sages' statement, which is the opposite of their previous state when they bowed to the idol as related in the Gemara41,
and afterwards, from this self-sacrifice, there is drawn down into the four letters of the Name Havayah,
light, joy, gladness, etc., and even to light, joy, gladness, and honor below ten handbreadths,
as the simple meaning of the verse.
